question:
From the given data, find the ratio of the cost prices of a shirt and a trouser.

 
 

 Item
 Selling Price
 Profit
 
 
 
 

 Shirt
 ₹1,200
 20%
 
 

 Trouser
 ₹660
 10%
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price of Shirt = 1200 × (100 ÷ 120) = ₹1000

Cost Price of Trouser = 660 × (100 ÷ 110) = ₹600

Ratio of their Cost Prices = 1000 : 600 = 5 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price of Shirt = ₹1,200 | Profit on Shirt = 20%

Selling Price of Trouser = ₹660 | Profit on Trouser = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [Selling Price × 100] ÷ [100 + Profit%]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00157e377959601fa2ca4f34cdea9c6186e75b533abd0436a52000cf462ff9c4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of Shirt = (1200 × 100) ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ CP of Shirt = 120000 ÷ 120 = ₹1000

⇒ CP of Trouser = (660 × 100) ÷ (100 + 10)

⇒ CP of Trouser = 66000 ÷ 110 = ₹600

⇒ Ratio of CPs = CP of Shirt : CP of Trouser

⇒ Ratio = 1000 : 600

⇒ Ratio = 5 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Formula

When an item is sold at a loss, the Cost Price is calculated as: CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%]

Marked Price and Discount

The Selling Price is determined by subtracting the discount percentage from the Marked Price (MP): SP = MP × [100 − Discount%] ÷ 100

Ratio Simplification

A ratio a : b essentially represents the fraction a ÷ b. It is always expressed in its simplest equivalent form by cancelling the Highest Common Factor among the values.
